subject: Customer: First-token jitter from CDN/TLS — exec update requested
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@brightretail.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, support@brightretail.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT spike: first-byte/jitter started last night (details attached)

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing significant first-token latency spikes overnight that are impacting our autocomplete UX and background inference jobs. p95 and p99 for first-token jumped ~2.5-4x across multiple routes starting ~2026-08-18T22:10Z. I attached a small Datadog snapshot and a short PCAP summary from our edge collector (handshake-pcap-brief.txt).

Symptoms:
- Increased TTFT (first token) p95 from ~280ms to ~1.1s; p99 to ~1.8s.
- Error rates are OK but throughput-backed queues are growing due to timeouts in callers.
- All traffic goes through FastEdge POPs (us-west-2 and us-east-1).

Can your team take an urgent look? This is impacting one of our peak flows and we've had a handful of revenue-impacting incidents today. Please escalate if this looks like CDN/TLS upstream behavior.

Thanks,
Janelle Park
Operations Lead, BrightRetail

Attachments:
- ttft-dash-20260819.png (png)
- handshake-pcap-brief.txt (text)
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@brightretail.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT spike: first-byte/jitter started last night (details attached)

Thanks for the heads-up, Janelle — I see the Datadog snapshot and pcap summary. We're escalating to SRE and networking immediately. Initial notes below and next steps.

Initial hypothesis:
- Symptoms line up with intermittent TLS handshake amplification at the CDN/edge (FastEdge) rather than model runtime regressions.
- The pcap shows repeated full-handshake patterns and delayed server hello timings from specific POPs.

Immediate actions we are taking:
1) Grace is pulling connection-level traces and correlation IDs for your traffic to identify which edges are most affected.
2) We're opening a ticket with FastEdge NOC and will provide pcap + timestamps.
3) We will test a temporary routing override to route your traffic to alternate POPs (if available) and/or force keepalive reuse.

Can you confirm the affected service endpoints and any geo constraints? Also, please send a list of example request IDs if you have them; will help trace on our side.

I'll follow up within 45 minutes with an initial triage update.

—Jonas
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BrightRetail TTFT spike — preliminary SRE findings

Team,

Quick triage summary from SRE/networking:
- We confirmed correlated spikes for BrightRetail traffic originating via FastEdge POPs in us-west-2 and us-east-1 between 2026-08-18T22:05Z and 2026-08-19T03:30Z.
- Packet captures show a rise in full TLS handshakes per connection (~+72% vs baseline) and an increase in server_hello RTTs from ~40ms to ~600ms on the affected POPs.
- No increase in model-side queue times or token-generation latency post-handshake once the stream is established. This strongly points to upstream (CDN/TLS) behavior.

Controllable mitigations we can deploy immediately:
A) Route override: force BrightRetail to alternate POPs in the same region (if FastEdge announces multiple POPs) OR route via our fallback edge region (latency trade-off).
B) Keepalive tuning: increase connection reuse and reduce full-handshake frequency for persistent clients.
C) Fallback model-variant routing to reduce token counts on the critical path while we stabilize.

Operational plan (next 24 hours):
- INF-4872 created (Jira) to track the issue and coordinate fixes with FastEdge: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4872
- I'll coordinate with FastEdge NOC and provide them the pcap and server-side traces (attached).
- If FastEdge provides a configuration patch window, we'll communicate an exact ETA.

I'll post a status update in 2 hours and will prepare an executive summary for the customer.

-Grace
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- handshake-pcap-brief.txt
From: Michael Kim <michael.kim@brightretail.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, janelle.park@brightretail.com
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT spike: first-byte/jitter started last night (details attached)

Jonas / Redwood execs,

This incident has materially impacted our checkout autocomplete and search. Our ops team has documented a revenue impact window of ~90 minutes during our Friday prime traffic. We need an executive-level timeline for a permanent resolution and a proposal for credits for the downtime.

Please provide:
- Confirmed root cause (CDN/TLS vs Redwood runtime) as you validate it.
- ETA for a durable fix and whether this will require coordination with FastEdge or configuration changes on Redwood.
- A proposed credit/SLA exception while we assess customer impact.

We'd also like to schedule a 30-minute call with your CTO/SRE head today if possible.

—Michael Kim
VP Engineering, BrightRetail
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Kim <michael.kim@brightretail.com>, janelle.park@brightretail.com
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Executive summary & next steps — BrightRetail TTFT incident (INF-4872)

Michael / Janelle — thank you for the patience. Executive summary below and immediate commitments from Redwood.

Summary of findings (validated):
- Root cause: transient TLS handshake amplification at FastEdge POPs (us-west-2 / us-east-1) causing elevated TTFT p95/p99 for BrightRetail. Our model runtime latency once the TLS session is established remained within SLOs.
- Evidence: Datadog dashboards, PCAP showing increased full-handshakes, and correlation of server_hello delays. See attached snapshot and the SRE brief.

Committed mitigations (today):
1) Route override applied for BrightRetail traffic to prefer alternate FastEdge POPs and our fallback edge for the next 48 hours. Monitoring in place; early signs show TTFT p95 improving toward baseline.
2) Keepalive/connection pooling parameters were tuned for your sessions to reduce full-handshake frequency.
3) Opened and are driving INF-4872 to track the long-term remediation with FastEdge; SRE will require FastEdge to share configuration patch and deployment ETA.

Proposed near-term remediation and credits:
- We propose an SLA exception/credit equivalent to 5% of billed usage during the 90-minute impact window while we finalize the FastEdge remediation. We will send a DocuSign SLA-exception form for signature: https://app.docusign.com/12345/SLA-exception-BR-2026-0793

Next steps:
- SRE will hold a customer call with BrightRetail NOC and FastEdge NOC at 18:00 UTC today to finalize patching timeline.
- I'll coordinate an exec sync between your VP and our SRE Head (evelyn_hart) now — available windows: 19:00 or 21:00 UTC.
- INF-4872 will be updated with all artifacts and the remediation timeline: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4872

Appreciate the urgency and we'll keep you updated in near real-time.

—Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
